data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO and found them to be standard VCS Go packaging with no malicious content. The only disagreement stems from the qwen model experiencing an API error (HTTP 400) when attempting to audit .gitignore, which is a tool failure rather than a security concern. The .gitignore file is a trivial AUR metadata file that ignores generated build artifacts - it contains no executable code and poses no security risk. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all three files and correctly identified the package as safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is caused by a tool error: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit .gitignore due to an HTTP 400 BadRequestError from the LLM API. This is not a genuine security disagreement but rather a coverage gap caused by infrastructure failure. The deepseek model successfully reviewed the same file and found it to be a standard AUR .gitignore with no security issues.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .gitignore due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: The audit tool should implement retry logic or graceful degradation when LLM API calls fail, rather than marking the entire audit as inconclusive due to a single file failure
For trivial files like .gitignore that contain no executable code, the tool could use pattern matching or simpler heuristics to avoid unnecessary LLM API calls and reduce failure points

When a model experiences a tool error on a non-critical file (like .gitignore), the verdict should not be blocked if all security-relevant files (PKGBUILD, .install, patches) were successfully reviewed
